reviews.title: Fantastic, User-Friendly Board for High-End Builds
reviews.comment:
I recently picked up the GIGABYTE X870E AORUS PRO for my new gaming PC, and I’m thoroughly impressed. First off, the board is incredibly good-looking; the sleek heatsinks and overall aesthetic give my build a very premium feel.
Assembly was a breeze thanks to the M.2 and PCIe EZ-Latch features, I didn't have to struggle with tiny screws or awkward latches while installing my components. It has been perfectly compatible with my Ryzen 7 9800X3D and DDR5 memory, offering rock-solid stability right out of the box. With the inclusion of PCIe 5.0 and plenty of high-speed ports, it feels like a great "future-proof" choice. This is a top-tier option for anyone looking for a reliable, easy-to-use, and high-performance AM5 motherboard.
reviews.author: Juan Camilo Uribe Martinez

reviews.title: Another great motherboard from Gigabyte
reviews.comment: Smooth process getting a new system together with this motherboard as the foundation. BIOS update was easy. Storage, memory, and CPU called out by the compatibilty sheets for this motherboard all integrated flawlessly. No connection issues. Probably the heaviest motherboard I have ever worked with and that's okay. Looks great in the case. For value, I was focused more on features than price and I'm happy with what I got.
reviews.author: John Raymonds

reviews.title: A worthy motherboard for future proofing
reviews.comment:
As prices for computer components continue to rise, PC builders are likely seeking an option that will last for the years to come. This is especially important for the component that is the most time consuming to swap in/out of your case. There are a number of features on this board that justify it's cost, particularly regarding it's attention to the upcoming market. There are three PCIe 5.0 M.2 slots. There are 3 ARGB LED headers, which is an appreciated amount, but certainly daisy chaining your fans or running a controller is still going to be necessary here. There rest of the connectors on the board and IO panel support the latest USB gens, including USB4. WIFI 7 is also included on this board, but while you may have considered the Elite WIFI 7 model, this PRO model has a 320hz channels whereas the ELITE only has 160hz.
The building experience on this board was a solid 10/10. They make it so much simpler to get parts in and out with the EZ latch mechanism. If you haven't worked with this in the past, there are plenty of tutorial videos from AORUS on youtube to reference as well. There are also a fair number of heatsinks on this board which is appreciated for someone looking to maximize their systems performance while keeping temperatures low.
The BIOS experience was also satisfactory, as AORUS offers two different interfaces for beginners only familiar with the basics, and experience enthusiasts looking to get the most out of their clocks. The individual options are plentiful and I have been able to easily find various settings things I needed to adjust (and then some).
In my opinion this motherboard stands amongst the best in terms of price to performance ratio. It certainly checked all the boxes for my current needs, but as I mentioned above, it's appeal is also to check the future boxes as well.
reviews.author: Jonathan Fischer

reviews.title: Excellent spec at decent price!
reviews.comment: Easy setup, with a high quality feel (this version has a full backplate installed which is nice addition). Paired with a 9950X3D and 32GB of DDR5 with Expo/XMP enabled to 6000MHz. Used in a workstation running multi-hour simulations with no issues.
reviews.author: O Jones

reviews.title: Nicely done.
reviews.comment:
I built a workstation with this board (not a gamer, a software developer). It is a great basis for the 9950x. One of my primary interests in this over other boards is 3 M.2 ports at Gen5 speeds, while others may only have 1 or 2.
Beware the details. DDR5 RAM requires training, and most boards seem locked up, unresponsive while it happens. I installed 96 Gbytes of RAM not on the "approved" list (though good quality). The time training requires is related to the size of the RAM, and faster RAM takes longer than slower RAM to train.
In my case the first boot looked like an RMA, either the RAM or the board made the first boot unresponsive for 15 minutes. That's a long time to sit, waiting, but it is training. No display, no sound, no change in the debug monitor (on board LED codes)...seems like it won't boot.
There are numerous threads on various boards discussing what people describe as a locked up computer on first build.
It is training.
Once it booted it never trained again. The resulting system is among the best workstations I've ever owned.
reviews.author: Jason Vene
